added_rules.name: Create titles on the fly
added_rules.description: DYNAMIC TITLE DISCOVERY (candidate directive 2026-10-18): the canonical title families are the floor, not the ceiling. During discovery in ANY lane, when you evaluate a posting whose title is NOT one of the run's current families, record it as a candidate in hidden_files/discovered-titles.json (create it as {"candidates": []} if absent): one entry per normalized title {title (as posted), postings (count of postings evaluated under this title), employers (distinct employer names), aligned (count of those postings whose FULL JD passed JD-first adjudication AND the experience-alignment test; a lead that fails only a gate fact — pay band, date, duplicate — counts as aligned when its duties aligned; a core experience-mismatch NEVER counts), first_seen, last_seen, runs (run ids)}. Update the entry on every evaluated posting carrying that title. Full JD reads only — never record a title from a snippet, a listing, or an unread JD. PROMOTION is deterministic, by the control actuator's maintenance pass — never by hand, never by editing lane-control.json: a candidate promotes into lane-control.json discovered_titles when postings >= 5 AND distinct employers >= 3 AND aligned == postings (every evaluated instance matched the candidate's experience), the title is not DevSecOps-titled, is not already a family (canonical, custom, or discovered), and is not in removed_titles; at most 3 promotions per day. A promoted title is on the candidate's list from then on: it joins the run's family set exactly like a canonical family in every lane (units derive for it, coverage is tracked per family by name) and stays until the candidate removes it (removed_titles). Purpose: titles carrying a lot of real postings that match his experience must not stay invisible just because they are not on the standing list — the odd-title net catches one-offs; this rule grows the list itself.
